item.title: SPNet: segmentation-to-poly network for building footprint extraction
item.dc:title: SPNet: segmentation-to-poly network for building footprint extraction
item.dc:creator: Huaigang Huang Ruisheng Wang Jinpeng Lei Kun Zhou Yibin Tian a School of Architecture and Urban Planning, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, Chinab State Key Laboratory of Subtropical Building and Urban Science, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, Chinac College of Mechatronics and Control Engineering, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, ChinaHuaigang Huang received the M.S. degree from the School of Geographic Science and Remote Sensing, Guangzhou University, in 2021. He is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree with the Department of Architecture and Urban Planning, Shenzhen University. His research interests include computer vision and intelligent extraction of remote sensing information.Ruisheng Wang (Senior Member, IEEE) received the B.Eng. degree from Wuhan University in 1993, the master’s degree from the University of New Brunswick in 2004, and the Ph.D. degree from McGill University in 2011. He is currently a Professor in the Department of Architecture and Urban Planning, Shenzhen University. His research interests include point cloud and computer vision, especially processing.Jinpeng Lei received his B.Eng. degree from the School of Surveying and Geo-Informatics Engineering, Henan Polytechnic University, in 2025. He is currently pursuing his M.Eng. degree in the Department of Architecture and Urban Planning, Shenzhen University, China. His research interests include computer vision.Kun Zhou received the B.Eng degree in information and computing science from Xiamen University of Technology in 2013, and the M.S. degree from Ningbo University in 2017. He is currently an Assistant Professor with the School of Architecture and Urban Planning, Shenzhen University. His research interests include 3D computer vision, image restoration, and neural rendering.Yibin Tian (Senior Member, IEEE) received the B.S. degree in Computer Applications from the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, the M.S. degree in Optical Engineering from Zhejiang University, and the Ph.D. degree in Vision Optics from the University of California. He also received the EMBA degree from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. He is currently a Professor in the Department of Mechanical and Control Engineering, Shenzhen University. His research interests include intelligent sensing and imaging, machine learning, optical and optoelectronic chips, precision manufacturing, and robotics applications.
